name: BMW S54B32 (E46 M3, 2000-2006)
summary: 3.2 L iron-block straight-six with six individual throttle housings fed from a common airbox plenum, 12 mm valve lift on both cams, double VANOS and an 8000 rpm limit; the individual throttles give a hard-edged induction rasp over the smooth six-cylinder exhaust.

rod_length_mm.note: Forged steel cracked rods; 21 mm wrist pin, 49 mm big-end journal.

crank.value: Forged steel, 7 main bearings (60 mm), 12 counterweights, 49 mm rod journals
crank.note: Pin angles are not stated in the document.

valves_per_cylinder.note: DOHC, finger followers with shim adjustment.

intake_lift_mm.note: Valve lift. The document says duration and lift (12 mm) of the lobes are the same on both camshafts.

intake_lobe_centre_range_deg.note: BMW 'spread angle' is the crank angle between TDC and maximum valve lift. VANOS moves the intake cam continuously over 60 deg; default mechanical stop is fully retarded (130 deg).

exhaust_lobe_centre_range_deg.note: VANOS moves the exhaust cam continuously over 45 deg; default mechanical stop is fully advanced (83 deg).

redline_rpm.note: Listed as 'Maximum Engine RPM'. Wikipedia also gives an 8000 rpm redline. A tuning site (https://bmwtuning.co/bmw-s54-engine/) lists 7900 rpm.

peak_power_kw.note: European E46 M3 (343 PS). US and Canada cars: 248 kW per Wikipedia; BMW's US training document gives 333 hp.

peak_torque_nm.note: European E46 M3. US cars: 355 Nm per BMW's US training document.

intake_type.value: individual throttles: six throttle housings operated by one electronic actuator, fed by a common plenum (airbox); idle air through a separate idle actuator and distribution pipe

header_type.value: two stainless steel manifolds (cylinders split into two groups), each with an integral catalytic converter on US cars
header_type.note: Which cylinders feed which manifold is not stated in the text.

exhaust_notes.value: E46 M3 exhaust is dual-channel as far as a single 40-litre half-shell rear silencer with four outlets.

missing: firing_order: no page opened states it for the S54 (search snippets showed 1-5-3-6-2-4 for other BMW sixes only)
intake_duration_deg and exhaust_duration_deg with the lift they are measured at (BMW gives only lift and lobe-centre range)
crank pin angles (120 degree six assumed by convention, not stated)

sources.what: BMW of North America technical training document 'M Engines - S54B32' (ST041 M3 Complete Vehicle, driveline section), hosted on the Internet Archive. Manufacturer training material: technical data table, rods, valves, cams, VANOS, intake and exhaust description.
Wikipedia S54 section: market-specific power and torque figures and redline.
Tuning-site overview; consulted only for the disagreeing 7900 rpm redline figure.

vehicle.name: BMW M3 coupé (E46, Europe, 2001)

curb_kg.note: 'Unladen weight to DIN ... M3 CSL 1385 | M3 Coupé 1495'. The US training document (https://archive.org/download/BMWTechnicalTrainingDocuments/ST041%20M3%20Complete%20Vehicle/1%20M3%20Complete%20Vehicle.pdf) agrees: 'Curb Weight, DIN 1495 kg'.

gears.note: 'Gear ratio, 1st gear 4.227 ... 2nd 2.528 ... 3rd 1.669 ... 4th 1.226 ... 5th 1.00 ... 6th 0.828 ... reverse 3.746'. US document; same ratios for European cars is my inference.

final_drive.note: BMW AG CSL manual technical data: 'Transmission M3 CSL M3 Sequential M gearbox (SMG) ... Final drive ratio 3.620:1'. The US document gives 'Rear Axle Differential Gear Ratio 3.64'. Which applies to the European manual car is not settled; 0.6 percent apart.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size 255/40 ZR18 (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio): unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius.

tyre.note: US running-gear training module: 'The sizes are 225/45 ZR 18 on the front and 255/40 ZR 18 on the rear.' Rear (driven) size used; European fitment assumed the same.

top_speed_kmh.note: 'Maximum speed km/h 250', footnote 'Electronically limited'. US document: 'Top Speed 155mph (governed)'.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'BMW M3' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front-engine, rear-wheel-drive (all-wheel drive only from 2021).

missing: a European BMW document giving the manual car's gear ratios, final drive and tyres
